akhfash:1-1.t: As for His words ﴿قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾, His word ﴿أَحدُ﴾ is a badal (substitute) for His word ﴿الله﴾, as if He said "He is One" (هُوَ أَحَدٌ). And among the Arabs are those who do not give it tanwīn, dropping it because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

akhfash:4-4.t: And His words ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ﴾: ﴿أَحَدٌ﴾ is the noun (ism of kāna) and ﴿كُفُوا﴾ is the khabar (predicate).

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿هُوَ﴾ the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of هو, and the clause «هو..» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿لَمْ يَلِدْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلَمْ يُولَدْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive imperfect verb in the jussive by lam, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam. ﴿لَهُ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) كفوا. ﴿كُفُواً﴾ the fronted khabar (predicate) of يكن. ﴿أَحَدٌ﴾ its postponed noun. The clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾.
They asked the Prophet ﷺ: What is your Lord? Does He eat or drink? Is He of gold or of silver? So Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, revealed: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ﴾. Then they said: What then is He? He said: ﴿أَحَدٌ﴾. This is among His attributes: that He is One (واحد). And «أحد», even though it is indefinite — Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: he means in its wording — is nominative by being made a fresh start (istiʾnāf), like His word: ﴿هَذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخٌ﴾. Al-Kisāʾī said something that I do not consider anything: he said: «هو» is an ʿimād (support pronoun), like His word: ﴿إِنَّهُ أَنَا اللهُ﴾. So he made «أحد» nominative by «الله», and made «هو» take the place of the hāʾ in (أنه). But an ʿimād is not begun with unless there is before it inna or one of its sisters, or kāna, or [verbs of] supposing.

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُفُواً أَحَدٌ﴾.
It is read heavy and light [i.e. «كُفُوًا» and «كُفْوًا»]. When the predicate (lit. "act") of the indefinite comes after it, it follows it [in case] with kāna and its sisters; so you say: لم يكن لعبدالله أحد نظير (ʿAbd Allāh has no one as an equal), [with «نظير» nominative]. When you put «النظير» first, they put it in the accusative and did not disagree on it, saying: لم يكن لعبدالله نظير أحد [Translator's note: printed without the accusative alif; the intended form is «نظيرًا»]. That is because when it comes after it, it follows the noun in its nominative; and when it comes first, there being nothing before it for it to follow, it reverts to the verb kāna and is made accusative.
The one who read "أحدُ اللهُ الصمدُ", dropping the nūn from (أحد), says: the nūn is the nūn of i'rab [i.e. the tanwīn]; when the alif and lām meet it, it is dropped. Likewise when a sākin (unvowelled letter) meets it, it is sometimes dropped, though that is not the [preferred] way. The readers have read: ﴿وقالت اليهود عُزَيْرُ ابنُ اللهِ﴾, and "عزيرٌ ابن الله".
Tanwīn is better. One of them recited to me:
لَتَجِدَنِّى بالأميرِ بَرّا * وبالقناةِ مِدْعَسًا مِكَرَّا * إذا غُطَيْفُ السُّلَمِىُّ فَرَّا *
(You will surely find me dutiful to the emir, and with the spear a hard thruster, charging again and again, when Ghuṭayf al-Sulamī runs away.)
And another recited to me:
كيْفَ نَومى على الفراشِ ولمّا * تَشْملِ الشَّامَ غارةٌ شعواءُ
تُذْهِلُ الشَّيخَ عن بَنيهِ وتُبدى * عن خِدامِ العقيلةُ العذراءُ
(How can I sleep on my bed when a far-flung raid has not yet engulfed Syria — one that makes the old man forget his sons, and makes the noble virgin uncover [her leg] from the anklet?)
He meant: عن خدامٍ, [with] العقيلةُ العذراءُ [as the subject]; and their saying [it is] عن خدامٍ [عقيلة] عذراء is nothing.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ هو اللَّهُ أحَدٌ﴾ ﴿اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ﴾ [al-Ikhlāṣ: 2] ("Say: He is Allah, One; Allah, the Eternal Refuge"), with tanwīn on ”أحَدٌ“. It was read without the tanwīn: ”أحَدُ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ“; and it was read with the dāl made vowelless and the tanwīn omitted. As for omitting the tanwīn, it is likewise because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, except that it is the vowellessness of two vowelless letters [Translator's note: so in the source, «سُكُون السّاكِنَيْنِ»; the text appears corrupt here]. Whoever makes it vowelless intends a pause, then begins anew and says: ﴿اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ﴾ [al-Ikhlāṣ: 2].
As for ”هو“: ”هُوَ“ is an allusion (kināya, pronoun) referring to the mention of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; the meaning is: "The One Whose lineage you asked to have made clear is Allah." And ”أحَدٌ“ is nominative on the sense ”هُوَ أحَدٌ هو اللَّهُ“ ("He is One; He is Allah"), so ”هُوَ“ is mubtadaʾ (subject). And ”هُوَ“ may be [the pronoun] of the matter (ḍamīr al-amr), as you say ”هُوَ زَيْدٌ قائِمٌ“, that is, "the matter is: Zayd is standing"; and the meaning is: "the matter is: Allah is One".

zajjaj:2-2.t:
And His saying: ﴿اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ﴾: it is related in the exegesis «that the polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Give us the lineage of your Lord", so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down: ﴿قُلْ هو اللَّهُ أحَدٌ﴾ [al-Ikhlāṣ: 1]». The explanation of ﴿الصَّمَدُ﴾ is: the lord in whom lordship culminates. The poet said:
لَقَدْ بَكَّرَ النّاعِي بِخَيْرَيْ بَنِي أسَدْ ∗∗∗ بِعَمْرِو بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ وبِالسَّيِّدِ الصَّمَدْ
(The announcer of death came early with [news of] the two best of Banū Asad: ʿAmr ibn Masʿūd and the lord, the ṣamad.)
And it was said: ”اَلصَّمَدُ“ is the one who has no hollow. And it was said: ”اَلصَّمَدُ“ is the one to whom everything turns (ṣamada lahu) [in need], and Who created all things, without Whom nothing can do; and all of them point to His oneness. All of these attributes may be applied to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أحَدٌ﴾ ("and there is none equal to Him"): there are four ways of reading in it: ﴿كُفُوًا﴾ with ḍamma on the kāf and the fāʾ; ”كُفْوًا“ with ḍamma on the kāf and sukūn on the fāʾ; ”كِفْوًا“ with kasra on the kāf and sukūn on the fāʾ, and it has been read so; and ”كِفاءً“ with kasra on the kāf. And ”اَلْكُفْءُ“, with fatḥa on the kāf [Translator's note: so in the source; the form printed has ḍamma] and sukūn on the fāʾ, is a noun; it was not read so. There is another way in it which is not permissible in reading. One says: ”فُلانٌ كُفْءُ فُلانٍ“ ("so-and-so is the equal of so-and-so"), like ”كُفِيُّ فُلانٍ“.
It has come in the ḥadīth «that ﴿قُلْ هو اللَّهُ أحَدٌ﴾ [al-Ikhlāṣ: 1] is equal to a third of the Qur'an, ﴿قُلْ يا أيُّها الكافِرُونَ﴾ [al-Kāfirūn: 1] is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an, and ﴿إذا زُلْزِلَتِ﴾ [al-Zalzala: 1] is equal to half of the Qur'an».
